scope: Three editorial illustrations for existing definition cards only.
standing: Conceptual illustrations, not Lab artifacts or evidence of actual operations.

images.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: a compact editorial illustration inside an HTML definition card for CyberAlchemy Lab.
Create a refined landscape image, about 3:2, designed to remain readable at 280 pixels wide.
Visual style: modern scientific field guide, crisp charcoal outlines, flat paper shapes with slight dimensional layering, restrained screenprint texture, no decorative clutter. Warm ivory background #faf7ef blending into an institutional article. Plenty of empty space around one compact, legible scene.
No words, letters, numbers, mathematical symbols, logos, watermark, caption, typography or illegible microtext anywhere. Real labels and the exact definition will be typeset in HTML beside the image.
No robot, brain, AI head, glowing circuit, neon, gradient blob, photograph, ornate poster, network hairball, dashboard screenshot or generic futuristic ornament.
The scene must explain the stated concept through visible relationships among concrete record objects; it is a conceptual illustration, not evidence of a successful outcome.
Scene: two paper record sheets stand side by side on a simple ivory desktop. The left sheet is a tidy source list of six teal row markers, visibly enclosed by a thin teal selection frame that represents a bounded subset. The right sheet is the saved export, with matching aligned row markers but one clear amber empty slot where a required row is absent. A fine, short comparison line links the two sheets. The sheets have precise lined rows, no writing. A tiny filter-shaped aperture at the source corner suggests that required rows are selected within an account and filter scope. Color: deep teal #23665f, charcoal, pale mint and a single amber omission. Do not show a checkmark, green success seal, an approval stamp or any implication that the incomplete export passed. Keep the illustration focused on required identifiers versus present identifiers, with the missing row instantly apparent.
